name: Claypot Chicken and Mushroom Rice
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source lists 691 cal / 38g protein. Rice cooks under the chicken so the whole dinner is one vessel - ideal for a 14-serving weigh-and-divide. Distinct from every existing rice bowl because the rice is cooked in the marinade, not served beside it. Confidence high. | HARVEST:
OVERRIDE Italian Seasoning: CANON-MAPPER FIX: '2 Chinese sausages (lap cheong)' = cured pork sausage ~75 g; nearest DB item Bratwurst
intro_html: Claypot chicken rice is one dish in one vessel. Marinated chicken, mushrooms, and sausage sit on top of the rice while it cooks, and everything they release drips down and seasons every grain. There is no separate protein and no separate side, which is why this lands so cheap. Each bowl carries {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1588 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 3.5 lb: ~$6.20. Buy 4 lbs: $7.08.
Oyster Sauce, 0.5 cups: ~$1.10. Buy 1 (covers about two batches).
Soy Sauce, 0.5 cups: ~$0.56. Buy 1 (covers about three batches).
Chicken Broth, 2.25 cups: ~$0.71. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Rice, 7.25 cups dry: ~$1.60. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.10. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $14.59 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.04 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $17.42 across 14 servings, roughly $1.24 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $11.54 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $28.96. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). That is not a typo and it is not a stripped down version of the dish. It is what happens when rice and chicken thighs do all the work and the flavor comes from sauces you already own.
shop_smart: Rice and boneless thighs are the two cheapest things you can build a dinner on, and this recipe is essentially both of them plus seasoning. That is the whole reason the per-bowl number is what it is.

Claypot rice traditionally uses Chinese sausage, or lap cheong. This build prices bratwurst because that is what an ordinary Omaha store actually stocks. Slice it thin and render it in the pan and it plays the same part for a lot less hunting.
Oyster sauce is a jar that lasts through many batches and it is doing most of the flavor work here. If your pantry has one Chinese ingredient, make it this one.

White mushrooms are cheaper than any specialty variety and they still release the savory liquid that flavors the rice. Buy the whole pack and slice them yourself, since pre-sliced costs more and dries out faster.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite sized pieces and marinate them with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, and a little salt and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms and the bratwurst thin. Thin matters, because everything on top needs to cook through in the same time the rice does.
Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then put it in a heavy pot or rice cooker with the chicken broth.
Lay the marinated chicken, mushrooms, and sausage across the top of the rice. Do not stir. The rice steams underneath while the toppings drip down into it, and stirring destroys the whole method.
Cook covered on low for about 25 minutes, or run a standard rice cooker cycle, then let it sit covered off the heat for 10 more minutes.
Lift the lid, pour any remaining marinade over the top, and now fold everything together gently.
Scatter the sliced green onions across the pot before portioning.
portion_html: Set the full pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Fold well before you scoop so the chicken and mushrooms are distributed evenly through the rice instead of sitting in a layer on top. Every container lands at {{cal}} calories.

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 3.5 lb (1588 g)
steps: Marinate the cut chicken thighs in oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sesame oil for 30 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms and bratwurst thin.
Rinse the rice and combine it with the chicken broth in a heavy pot or rice cooker.
Lay the chicken, mushrooms, and sausage on top without stirring and cook covered about 25 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes, fold everything together, top with green onions, and portion into 14 containers.
